meta.title: En-Path Discovery - Native FigJam Content
meta.purpose: Compact source-of-truth dataset for rebuilding all six sections as editable FigJam objects.
content_rules: Use one editable sticky or text card per card object.
Use editable connectors for every relationship object.
HR Admin content remains a role-based draft because no validated HR Admin persona exists.
Do not imply reminders, deadlines, notification channels, an SLA, or a scoring formula.

sections.title: PVB
sections.subtitle: Product Vision Board
sections.layout: Five horizontal groups: Vision, Target Groups, Business Goals, Needs, Product Principles.

cards.title: En-Path Vision
cards.body: For enterprise HR leadership managing competencies, assessments, and career paths across disconnected spreadsheets. En-Path turns evaluation into explainable employee profiles, development priorities, and role-qualification decisions.

cards.title: Single Auditable Standard
cards.body: Unlike fragmented tools and opaque assessments, En-Path centralizes skills, evaluations, role requirements, career gaps, and decision history in one transparent source of truth.

cards.title: Employee
cards.body: Early-career, mid-career, and experienced employees, both tech-savvy and non-tech-savvy, who want to own their career growth and professional development.

cards.title: HR / L&D
cards.body: Junior through senior HR and L&D professionals who design, manage, and optimize talent-development programs and organizational capability.

cards.title: Manager / Leader
cards.body: New team leads through senior department leaders who manage workforce capability, team performance, and strategic talent decisions.

cards.title: Employee Goal
cards.body: Understand current capabilities, identify competency gaps, and take ownership of growth toward a desired role.

cards.title: HR / L&D Goal
cards.body: Build consistent competency metrics, define transparent career paths, and govern evidence-based evaluation and development.

cards.title: Manager Goal
cards.body: Evaluate workforce capability transparently, make accountable role-readiness decisions, and close gaps through targeted development.

cards.title: Employee Need
cards.body: Clear current level and progression, target-role requirements, personalized next actions, and one place for competencies, certifications, courses, and achievements.

cards.title: Team Leader Need
cards.body: A fast, reliable view of team competencies, gaps, evidence, and development plans for coaching and objective review conversations.

cards.title: Strategic Manager Need
cards.body: Organization-wide capability insight for workforce planning, succession, promotions, future skill demand, and organizational gap analysis.

cards.title: Product Promise
cards.body: Every competency score and career decision should be transparent, explainable, and reusable throughout the employee lifecycle.

cards.title: Trust Foundation
cards.body: Use shared competency standards, evidence and rationale, authorized verification, auditable history, and appropriate access controls.

sections.title: Product Canvas
sections.subtitle: MVP scope, value loop, personas, measures, and guardrails
sections.layout: Canvas grid with Product Goal at top, Personas at left, MVP Capabilities in the center, Measures and Guardrails at right.

cards.title: Problem
cards.body: Competencies, reviews, experience, and career paths are fragmented. Employees cannot see their current state, important gaps, or next actions, and agreed actions are often forgotten between reviews.

cards.title: MVP Outcome
cards.body: Target -> gap -> roadmap and next actions -> follow-up -> evidence and review -> verified competency -> updated roadmap. Used throughout the employee's tenure.

cards.title: Role in Performance Reviews
cards.body: En-Path does not replace performance or promotion decisions. It replaces manual data collection and turns reviews into evidence-based calibration checkpoints.

cards.title: Employee
cards.body: Understand the current level, select a target, demonstrate competency, request reviews, execute a development plan, revisit agreed actions, and reuse a visual career profile.

cards.title: Manager
cards.body: Understand each employee's capability, clarify promotion direction, agree and follow up actions, verify evidence, update plans, and make staffing decisions.

cards.title: HR Admin
cards.body: Set up roles, levels, competency matrices, and career paths; publish shared competency metrics; monitor gaps and progress by role and level.

cards.title: Competency Standard
cards.body: Maintain competency metrics and career paths by role and level as the comparison standard.

cards.title: Profile, Target, and Gap
cards.body: Provide a career profile, target role or level, gap analysis, prioritized development needs, and a publishable or exportable profile.

cards.title: Roadmap and Retained Actions
cards.body: Store the development roadmap, agreed next actions, follow-up status, and jointly confirmed action history so commitments are not lost.

cards.title: Continuous Evidence Review
cards.body: Capture evidence and rationale, support event-based review requests, authorize verification, and retain immutable competency history.

cards.title: Updated Views and Reuse
cards.body: Update competency, gaps, readiness, roadmap, and Manager team view; let Employees export or publish the verified career profile.

cards.title: Clarity and Trust
cards.body: Employees understand gaps against company direction and can identify the next action. Managers can interpret evaluation results and outcomes through a shared view.

cards.title: Employee Activation
cards.body: An Employee has a target role or level, has an available gap analysis, and reaches a first roadmap quickly.

cards.title: Business Rules and Manual MVP Work
cards.body: Verified skills require an authorized reviewer plus evidence or rationale. Least-privilege access and immutable history apply. HR and Managers manually map gaps to assignments, mentors, materials, or courses.

cards.title: Assumptions and Constraints
cards.body: Pilot one career family with a complete owned matrix. Managers will run short event-based reviews. Rule-based recommendations are sufficient. Competency-metric quality and Manager workload determine reliability.

cards.title: Later Phases
cards.body: Peer workflows, advanced organizational analytics, HRIS or LMS integration, multiple targets, competency-metric versioning, and AI recommendations.

sections.title: Personas
sections.subtitle: Validated Employee and Engineering Manager personas
sections.layout: Two side-by-side persona columns, each with Profile, Goals, Needs, and Pain Points.

cards.title: Profile
cards.body: Age 20-25; Backend Engineer; male. Early-career, technically focused, proactive about learning, and seeking clear progression plus recognition from real project work.

cards.title: Goals
cards.body: Understand current skills and experience; identify target-role gaps; assess promotion or internal-mobility readiness; track growth; build a practical personalized career path.

cards.title: Needs and Expectations
cards.body: Continuous skill updates from project contributions, Manager validation, transparent gap analysis, practical learning recommendations, and visible next-role requirements.

cards.title: Pain Points
cards.body: Updates wait for periodic reviews; current levels and priorities are unclear; promotion readiness is hard to judge; project contributions may be missed; next-level requirements lack visibility.

cards.title: Profile
cards.body: Age 25-35; Engineering Manager; male. Coaches through projects and 1:1s, values evidence-based development, understands technical role expectations, and balances people growth with delivery.

cards.title: Goals
cards.body: Track team skill growth; support career plans and mobility; capture continuous feedback; prepare better reviews; identify shared gaps; build team capability.

cards.title: Needs and Expectations
cards.body: Centralized skill records and evidence, employee-initiated review requests, Manager validation, historical review context, tracked development plans, gap analysis, and practical growth actions.

cards.title: Pain Points
cards.body: No dedicated competency tool; evidence gathering is manual; records and history are scattered; mobility planning is unclear; assessments are infrequent; 1:1 actions are lost; Employees cannot request structured reviews.

sections.title: Customer Journey Maps
sections.subtitle: Employee, Manager, and HR Admin role journeys
sections.layout: Three horizontal lanes. Place stages left-to-right inside each lane and use cross-lane handoffs where specified.

cards.title: 1. Understand Current Profile
cards.body: Review skills, experience, strengths, and development areas. Outcome: a clear current competency state instead of fragmented history.

cards.title: 2. Select Target and See Gaps
cards.body: Choose a target role or level, compare against company metrics, and identify priority gaps. Outcome: clear direction and requirements.

cards.title: 3. Agree on Roadmap
cards.body: Discuss target, gaps, and next actions in a 1:1 with the Manager. Store a shared roadmap that both parties can revisit.

cards.title: 4. Execute and Follow Up
cards.body: Act through projects and daily work, record progress and evidence, then revisit and jointly confirm previous action statuses instead of losing them until the next review.

cards.title: 5. Request Evidence Review
cards.body: After a project or development event, submit evidence and rationale for authorized competency review. Outcome: recognition can occur continuously and transparently.

cards.title: 6. Receive Updated State
cards.body: View verified competencies, changed gaps, readiness, roadmap, and next actions. Outcome: the profile reflects real progress and guides the next cycle.

cards.title: 7. Export or Publish Profile
cards.body: Reuse a consistent profile containing personal information, work history, and experience for interviews or client pitches.

cards.title: 1. Understand Team Capability
cards.body: Review the Employee List, current skills, gaps, evidence, and development history under one shared standard instead of consolidating multiple sources.

cards.title: 2. Clarify Direction
cards.body: Use the Employee profile, target requirements, and gap analysis to clarify readiness and priority development needs.

cards.title: 3. Roadmap and Follow-Up
cards.body: Agree on actions, coach progress, then compare evidence with previous commitments, jointly confirm statuses, and agree what comes next.

cards.title: 4. Receive and Verify Review
cards.body: Receive an event-based request and, when authorized, assess the evidence and rationale. Outcome: an auditable competency decision.

cards.title: 5. Adjust Roadmap
cards.body: Use updated competencies and gaps to continue coaching and update development actions to match the new state.

cards.title: 6. Plan and Select Staff
cards.body: Use the Employee List, current skills, and gap analysis to consider suitable people for a project or client pitch.

cards.title: 1. Establish Metrics
cards.body: Define roles, levels, competency matrices, and career paths as a sufficiently complete shared standard.

cards.title: 2. Publish Metrics
cards.body: Finalize and publish the standard used by profiles, targets, Manager views, and gap analyses.

cards.title: 3. Monitor Gaps and Progress
cards.body: Track competency gaps and progress by role and level against the published standard. Persona motivations remain unvalidated.

sections.title: User Story Map
sections.subtitle: Discovery backbone and MVP value slices
sections.layout: Eight backbone columns from left to right, with four release-slice cards below and two boundary cards at the side.

cards.title: 1. Establish Competency Metrics
cards.body: HR Admin sets up roles, levels, matrices, and career paths, then publishes competency metrics. The system stores them as the shared standard.

cards.title: 2. Understand Profiles and Team
cards.body: Employee views profile, work history, strengths, and development areas. Manager views Employee List, skills, gaps, evidence, and history. HR tracks gaps by role and level.

cards.title: 3. Select Target and Understand Gaps
cards.body: Employee selects a target role or level. The system compares the current profile with target metrics and identifies priority gaps; Manager clarifies direction.

cards.title: 4. Roadmap, Actions, and Follow-Up
cards.body: Employee and Manager agree actions, execute them, revisit previous statuses, jointly confirm progress, and agree next actions. The system retains the full shared history.

cards.title: 5. Evidence and Review Request
cards.body: Employee records project evidence and rationale, then submits an event-based review request. Manager receives evidence in roadmap context; the system centralizes it.

cards.title: 6. Verify and Update Competencies
cards.body: An authorized reviewer assesses evidence. The system stores immutable results with least-privilege access and updates competencies, gaps, readiness, and roadmap.

cards.title: 7. Reuse Profile and Data
cards.body: Employee exports or shares a profile for interviews or pitches. Manager uses current skills and gaps for project staffing or client pitching.

cards.title: 8. Track Gaps and Progress
cards.body: HR tracks progress by role and level; Manager maintains team capability context; Employee continues the target-to-review development cycle.

cards.title: Slice 0 - Foundation / Pilot
cards.body: One career family has an owned, sufficiently complete matrix and published metrics. Store the standard and enforce least-privilege access. Open: initial profile source and HR persona.

cards.title: Slice 1 - Career Clarity
cards.body: Employee gets a profile, target, priority gaps, first roadmap, and retained next actions. Manager gets basic team visibility; learning mapping remains manual.

cards.title: Slice 2 - Closed Review Loop
cards.body: Employee and Manager revisit and confirm actions; evidence triggers review; an authorized reviewer verifies competency; the system updates the profile and roadmap.

cards.title: Slice 3 - Profile and Staffing Reuse
cards.body: Employee exports or publishes the updated profile. Manager reuses Employee List, skills, and gaps for project or pitch consideration.

cards.title: Outside Current MVP
cards.body: Peer workflow, advanced organization analytics, HRIS or LMS integrations, multiple career targets, competency-metric versioning, and AI-generated recommendations.

cards.title: Open Before Epics and Stories
cards.body: Initial profile source; scoring and readiness; reviewer assignment; rejected evidence and disputes; project-fit rules; public-profile privacy; next-action statuses; SLA and notifications; HR Admin persona. PRD, architecture, and UX are still prerequisites.

sections.title: Cross-Role Swimlane
sections.subtitle: Handoffs among HR Admin, Employee, Manager, and En-Path
sections.layout: Four horizontal lanes with aligned left-to-right stages. Use solid arrows for flow and dashed arrows for reuse or iteration.

cards.title: Establish Standard
cards.body: Set up roles, levels, competency matrices, and career paths.

cards.title: Publish Metrics
cards.body: Publish competency metrics as the shared organizational standard.

cards.title: Monitor Adoption
cards.body: Track gaps and progress by role and level. HR persona remains undefined.

cards.title: View Profile and Select Target
cards.body: Understand current competencies and choose a target role or level.

cards.title: Understand Priority Gaps
cards.body: Review the comparison between current profile and target requirements.

cards.title: Agree on Roadmap
cards.body: Agree next actions with the Manager after a 1:1.

cards.title: Execute and Follow Up
cards.body: Act, create evidence, revisit previous actions, jointly confirm statuses, and agree what comes next.

cards.title: Request Competency Review
cards.body: Submit evidence and rationale after a project or development event.

cards.title: Use Updated Profile
cards.body: View verified competency, readiness, and roadmap; export or publish the profile for interviews or pitches.

cards.title: View Team and Clarify Direction
cards.body: Use the Employee List, skills, gaps, and history to clarify target and development priorities.

cards.title: Co-Own Roadmap and Follow-Up
cards.body: Agree actions, coach progress, review evidence, and jointly confirm previous statuses with the Employee.

cards.title: Verify Competency
cards.body: When authorized, assess evidence and rationale and make an auditable verification decision.

cards.title: Coach and Reuse Data
cards.body: Adjust the roadmap, start the next development cycle, and use skills and gaps for staffing or client pitching.

cards.title: Store Published Metrics
cards.body: Keep the shared standard for profiles, targets, team views, and gap analysis.

cards.title: Compare and Generate Gaps
cards.body: Compare current profile with target metrics and identify priority gaps.

cards.title: Persist Roadmap and Status History
cards.body: Retain roadmap, next actions, progress, jointly confirmed statuses, and subsequent actions.

cards.title: Store Evidence and Request
cards.body: Centralize evidence, rationale, and the event-based review request.

cards.title: Store Verification and Update State
cards.body: Keep immutable decision history with least-privilege access; update profile, gaps, readiness, and roadmap.
